# SlowGo

> Navigation for golf carts and low-speed vehicles. SlowGo builds routes that stay
> on roads posted 35 mph and under wherever possible, and says so plainly when a
> trip can't avoid something faster. A product of BackRoad Apps LLC.

SlowGo is pre-launch. The iOS app is expected in summer 2026; there is no App Store
listing yet, and the site currently collects waitlist signups. Android comes later.

## Status and coverage

- Routing is live in **Florida and Georgia** only. Those two states are where
  SlowGo's speed-limit data is checked today.
- Outside Florida and Georgia you can search, browse the map, and plan a ride,
  but SlowGo will not start a turn-by-turn route. States are added one at a time,
  after their roads are checked, rather than guessed at.
- Built with cart communities in mind — The Villages, Hilton Head, Peachtree City,
  Fire Island, and similar places.

## How routing works

- **Green** — roads posted 35 mph and under. This is the default, and most rides
  never leave it.
- **Amber** — roads posted 36 to 45 mph. Offered only if the rider opts in to
  faster stretches, and the length of the stretch is shown before the ride starts.
- **NoGo** — no route exists that stays on 35-and-under roads. SlowGo says so
  rather than quietly routing onto a fast road.
- Roads posted above 45 mph are not offered.

## Privacy posture

- No accounts, no sign-in, no ads, no ad tracking.
- Route requests are processed on a first-party server and are not kept beyond
  short-lived technical logs.
- Favorites and trip history stay on the device. Trip start and end points are
  stored roughly, not precisely.
